\TThe wear index of the clutch since the last time the clutch adaption was reset. Typical values are between -2000 and 12000. Over time this value increases. Higher values indicate more advanced wear.

Name.Text: Position of clutch slip point, 0 Nm transmission

Messwert.Meldungstext: \TThe clutch slip point is the so-called \L\B\K\N<kiss point>\L\S\K\N at which the clutch is closed but no power is yet being transmitted (0 Nm). Typical values are between 380 and 600.
\TPoint at which the clutch is fully closed for the current driving cycle. This value is stored following adaption of the clutch.

Name.Text: Position: clutch fully closed (current driving cycle)

Messwert.Meldungstext: \TPoint at which the clutch is fully closed. The value originates from the current driving cycle and should vary only to a small extent from the adapted value.

\TWhen the engine is off the clutch is fully closed and values between 1000 - 1700 occur. With a new clutch this value with the clutch closed is around 1000. Over the lifetime this value increases due to abrasion.

\T\Y\F\J\N Y\Y\S\J\NZ\L\S\K\INote: The temperature is based on an arithmetic model.
At temperatures above 200°C, in gear 1 the clutch is closed quickly. Above 300°C the clutch opens, accompanied by a warning on the dash.
